newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz ties up loose ends on Hermes bid.
newsitem.headline: Allianz ties up loose ends on Hermes bid.

text.p: German insurance giant Allianz AG Holding on Tuesday launched a bid for outstanding shares in loan insurer Hermes Kreditversicherungs AG in a move to tie up loose ends from its complicated share swap last year.
In an advertisement carried in the business daily Handelsblatt, Allianz said it would pay 385 marks ($242) per outstanding Hermes share in an offer running from January 20 through March 20.
In a separate announcement, the Allianz-controlled Vereinte Holding group launched an offer for the same period for remaining shares in Vereinte Versicherungs AG.

The bids are a follow-up to a surprise deal Allianz struck last July with reinsurer Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG, which built up its stake in Vereinte Versicherung to some 98 percent and gave it 75.3 percent of Hermes, a key player in credit insurance.

Allianz said at the time that it meant to make offers for the remaining shares in both units -- in the final touches to a deal which saw it unexpectedly offload its DKV health insurance unit to satisfy cartel office concerns about its dominance in the sector, in which Vereinte also plays a major role.
Both Allianz and Vereinte said the management boards of both smaller units had been informed of the offer conditions.
Hermes' management board considered the offer "reasonable", according to Allianz.

Hermes shares last closed on their home Hamburg stock exchange at 380 marks, but Allianz said its bid represented a premium of 30 percent on the price at which they were trading before the takeover was announced.
Moreover, Allianz said it would make additional payments to shareholders who took up this initial offer in the event that it should subsequently up its bid before March 27 1998.

Vereinte, meanwhile, said it was offering Vereinte Versicherung shareholders a 20 percent premium on the price their shares traded last July and said the company's management was recommending that they avail themselves of the offer.

The Vereinte bid breaks down as follows: 2,850 marks per bearer share with a par value of 100 marks, 1,050 marks for registered shares with par value of 50 marks and 2,100 marks per registered share with par value of 100 marks.
Last July, Allianz said only around two percent of Vereinte Versicherung shares was still held by small investors. ($ = 1.588 German Marks)
